identity.name: coa
identity.description: Loads Committee of Adjustment applications from two Toronto Open Data CKAN DataStore resources (Active always; Closed since 2017 in full mode only), one union group (R-DX (iii)/(iv)) on coa_applications: a data_hash-guarded upsert on application_number with the last_seen_at touch for every fed key (R-DZ), and one derived lifecycle_status_history row per status change from the runner's prior-status read (R-DY), non-fatal (R-DM).

why_lock.text: Spec 47 §A.5 lock registry row 95; the legacy ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 95 wrapped the whole run in withAdvisoryLock [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:432-435]; the shell keeps the constant as a §5.4 source-text literal.

why.text: The legacy upsert is change-guarded by WHERE coa_applications.data_hash IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.data_hash [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:316-333]; data_hash covers every mapped column, so it is the one guard column. last_seen_at is the written "seen" column (Spec 124 R-DZ): inserted, set on conflict, excluded from the guard and touched for every fed key inside the same transaction, which closes COA-D4 (the legacy touch ran on the pool after the batches [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:565-583]). One transaction for the target in R-CU slices; the legacy per-500-row transaction form is not carried (Spec 124 R-DY (d): no per-batch transaction form, coa_batch_size is not seeded).

Spec 124 R-DY, operator decision 2 (2026-10-17): the legacy read SELECT application_number, status FROM coa_applications WHERE application_number = ANY($1) before each batch upsert [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:255-264] and wrote one ledger row per application whose CKAN status differs from the stored one [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:351-377]. The runner now reads that prior state per slice inside the primary transaction and hands it to the pure compute export deriveRows.

on_error_why.text: Spec 124 R-DM (operator y 2026-10-17): the legacy wrapped the ledger INSERT in SAVEPOINT ledger_write and on failure rolled back to it, kept the upsert and counted ledgerErrorCount = 1 [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:380-426]. The runner's SAVEPOINT sp_e1 does the same per slice and counts written.e1.errors, which the declared WARN check lifecycle_status_history_errors bounds at viol == 0.

why.text: The shared natural-key ON CONFLICT of the three ledger writers [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:389-401]: ON CONFLICT (lead_id, to_status, date_trunc('second', transitioned_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')) DO UPDATE event_date only when the new value is non-null and differs. The conflict target is probed from the unique index uniq_lifecycle_status_history_natural_key (migrations/127_create_lifecycle_status_history.sql:58; Spec 124 R-DY (c)), and event_date on_empty "preserve_null" renders the legacy non-null-and-different guard.

Four generated statements per R-CU slice inside the one transaction (Spec 124 R-DY (a)): the prior-status read, the guarded coa_applications upsert, the last_seen_at touch for every fed key (R-DZ) and the derived lifecycle_status_history upsert.

Migration 227 enabled RLS on coa_applications with ZERO policies (relrowsecurity=true, 0 policies [MEASURED 2026-10-17, assessment §1.5]); under a non-bypass role the upsert affects 0 rows with no error (trap 2, Spec 124 R-CT).
RLS is on for lifecycle_status_history with zero policies [MEASURED 2026-10-17, assessment §1.5]; a non-bypass role would drop every ledger row silently (Spec 124 R-CT).
coa_applications.lead_id is trigger-maintained (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF application_number); the ledger rows key on coa:<application_number> = that lead_id (R-BL(iii)).

batch_why.text: Generated (scripts/generate-ingest-batch.js, FLEET-2 B-3 #37): a step with two write targets declares "none" — the runner slices each target at its own write stride (pipeline.maxRowsPerInsert, Spec 124 R-CU), and the derived lifecycle_status_history rows ride the primary slice (R-DY (a)). The legacy BATCH_SIZE 500 per-batch transaction is not carried (R-DY (d)).

on_row_error_why.text: A record with a blank REFERENCE_FILE# is the runner's counted bad key (legacy skip reason missing_app_num [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:179-180]); a record missing a CRITICAL field is shaped as schema_mismatch. The tolerance is the FAIL check skip_rate.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a value the runner already measured (rows_read, rows_shaped, bad_key_count, column_nulls, the write counters) or one declared SELECT, so a check that throws is a defect, not an upstream condition — it must redden the run.

why.text: COA-D7: the legacy loader ran VACUUM ANALYZE coa_applications on every run [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:600-602]; runMaintenance gates it on coa_applications_dead_tuple_ratio_warn_max (seeded 0, so any dead tuple triggers it, the faithful form of the unconditional legacy run) and runs it autocommit after the write — the load_massing / load_neighbourhoods form.

Zero records from CKAN is a WARN run that writes nothing — possible API outage or empty dataset [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:465-486]; the legacy SKIPPED status/reason rows become this one zero-tolerance row (COA-D14).

order_guarantee.guarantee: A CKAN record missing a CRITICAL field fails the run before any write to coa_applications or lifecycle_status_history.
order_guarantee.anchor: schema drift: the run fails before any write

why.text: A CKAN record missing a CRITICAL field aborted the legacy run before any write [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:171-177, :515-533]. The observer reads each selected member's acquired header (acquired.members[id].record_fields, the CKAN arm's first-record keys; CKAN DataStore records carry the full field set) and the records shaped as schema_mismatch; zero tolerance, scored by the runner's pre_write gate, so a FAIL means no write at all.

expect.of: days from the newest hearing on/before the run date to the run clock

why.text: Portal rot. Legacy WARN at >= 45 days from max(hearing_date) [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:587-590, :626]. COA-D6, operator-ruled 2026-10-17 (decision 4): measured from the newest hearing ON/BEFORE the run date among the rows this run fed — the rows at MAX(last_seen_at), which R-DZ touches for every fed key inside the write transaction — so a future-scheduled hearing no longer hides staleness. COA-D2: the log line's > 45 retires; the bound is coa_max_days_stale_warn in the inclusive value_max form (declared deviation).

Spec 37 tripwire: WARN the moment CONTACT_NAME data reappears — the build signal for the deferred CoA entity extraction [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:627-635]. Counted pre-dedup over the mapped records (shapeRecord tags applicant_present; acquired.shaped_tags), as the legacy mapped.filter.

WARN only when EVERY written row has no zoning_designation — the signature of a CKAN rename of ZONING_DESIGNATION [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:636-637]. Read from acquired.column_nulls.zoning_designation over acquired.feature_count (the deduplicated rows, as the legacy deduplicated.every); the null count is the row detail.

Legacy INFO row: the ledger INSERT's rowCount [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:411, :641] = written.e1.inserted + written.e1.updated (Spec 124 R-DY (e) counters of the derived target).

Spec 124 R-DM: a failed lifecycle_status_history slice rolls back to the runner SAVEPOINT sp_e1, the coa_applications upsert is kept, and written.e1.errors counts it; this row WARNs on any [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:415-426, :642].

Spec 124 R-DE (iv): an INGESTOR emits ONE <x>_load object, so the data_health block is records_meta.coa_load (same fields; max_days_stale is the check row of that name); api_health and duration_ms are runner telemetry. Measured readers of coa data_health: none outside the step (grep 2026-10-18).

deviations.adjudicated_by: Spec 124 R-DC (124:236, the inclusive ceiling_max form, operator y 2026-10-17) — the assert_coa_freshness ACF-D7 precedent (W4A-R2)

why.text: COA-D6: a future-scheduled hearing (live max 2027-10-08) clamped the value to 0, so portal rot was undetectable; now the newest hearing on/before the run date.

why.text: Spec 124 R-DY (d): one transaction per target in R-CU slices, no per-batch transaction form (coa_batch_size is not seeded); R-DZ moves the touch inside that transaction (COA-D4). An interruption now leaves nothing half-written.

deviations.from: MAX_RETRIES 3 attempts with exponential backoff RETRY_BASE_MS * 2^(n-1) [READ src/tests/steps/coa/fixtures/legacy-load-coa.js.txt:34-35, :108-136]

why.text: The runner CKAN arm retries coa_download_retries times after the first attempt with a linear backoff_ms * attempt (acquire.js acquireCkanDatastore); seeded 2 retries / 2000 ms, the waits are 2000 then 4000 ms — identical to the legacy three attempts. GR-3 adds a named refusal when fetched != result.total.

deviations.adjudicated_by: load_zoning precedent (runner acquisition owns retries, R-DX ckan_datastore primary)

limitations.what: COA-D11: data_hash takes dates in the UTC-midnight ISO form (YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000Z), identical to the legacy under a UTC process. The legacy read the zone-less Closed FINALDATE through Date.parse in the PROCESS TimeZone, so hashes written by an America/Toronto process differ: the first converted --full on such a database re-upserts those Closed rows once (status unchanged, so no ledger row). Incremental (Active-only) runs are unaffected: a YYYY-MM-DD date parses as UTC in both forms.
limitations.measured: dev DB vs live CKAN, read-only 2026-10-19: 31,253 of 31,270 Closed rows hash in the America/Toronto form, 0 in the UTC form (17 are live CKAN changes); 2,628 of 2,675 Active rows hash identically in both forms (47 are live CKAN changes) [MEASURED, scratchpad parity-tz.js]

limitations.what: Rows that leave the feed are never retired; last_seen_at is the only departure signal (assert_coa_freshness).

interrupted_why.text: The coa_applications upsert, the last_seen_at touch and the derived ledger rows commit in one transaction (Spec 124 R-DY (d)); an interrupted run commits nothing and a rerun writes only what changed (data_hash guard).

before_image_why.text: A guarded upsert of a published feed; the CKAN resources are the before-image.
